cohort: A male extremely low birth weight, growth-restricted preterm infant born at 27 weeks gestation, who developed fulminant late-onset sepsis due to Staphylococcus lugdunensis.
finding: Staphylococcus lugdunensis can cause fulminant late-onset sepsis with persistent bacteremia secondary to an infected aortic thrombus in extremely low birth weight preterm infants, representing a rare presentation.
followup_time: Observation until recovery, including a 6-week course of intravenous antibiotics and a 4-week course of anticoagulant therapy.
birth_weight: extremely low birth weight (specific weight not mentioned)
